standard_prerequisites.name: The construction of the morphism into a projective bundle associated with a degree one generating set of a graded algebra, which is a closed immersion when the symmetric algebra surjects onto the algebra, cited from the constructions chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the closed immersion of the relative Proj into the projective bundle of the degree one part, which is the claim.

core_obligations: Identify the map: the graded algebra is generated in degree one over its degree zero part, so the canonical map from the symmetric algebra on the degree one part onto the algebra is surjective (proof lines 7812-7816).

Apply the construction: by the cited statement the associated morphism of relative Proj's is a closed immersion into the projective bundle of the degree one part, and since that degree one part is a finite type module over the base, this expresses the relative Proj as a closed subscheme of a projective bundle over the base, i.e. it is projective (proof lines 7816-7822).
proof_roadmap: Use the surjection from the symmetric algebra on the degree one part to get the closed immersion into the projective bundle, which gives projectivity (proof lines 7812-7822).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that the relative Proj of a graded algebra generated in degree one by a finite type module is a projective morphism (statement lines 7802-7810). The counted proof is short and complete: generation in degree one means the canonical map from the symmetric algebra on the degree one part is surjective, so by the cited construction the relative Proj embeds as a closed subscheme of the projective bundle of the degree one part, which is a projective bundle over the base because that module is of finite type (proof lines 7812-7822). It is H2: the reduction is carried out in the counted span and the cited input is the standard closed immersion of relative Proj's induced by a surjection from a symmetric algebra.
